title: Pre-Analysis — Retrofit of the Trimmable Horizontal Stabiliser Front Spar Attachment Fitting Standard
abstract: Pre-analysis of bringing in-service ZEPHYR-24 aircraft to the forged front spar attachment fitting standard, covering the tail cone work it collides with, the bulkhead inspections it displaces and the wiring that crosses the same area.

sections.objective: Establish what a retrofit of the forged attachment fitting standard would involve on an aircraft in service, as opposed to the production cut-in already achieved. The fitting change was released against a design service goal extension, and the operators with the highest utilisation are the ones that want it first. Pre-analysis was asked to identify every other activity that needs the same tail cone access, and to say whether the retrofit can be built as a single deep maintenance package rather than a standalone campaign.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and the picture that emerged is one of shared access rather than conflict. The retrofit needs the rear pressure bulkhead area open, which is also where a candidate web doubler would work, and the two share a machined fitting item; if the doubler is launched the two must be sequenced deliberately because the doubler changes the surface the fitting jig registers against. The scheduled bulkhead inspection occupies the same access and the same inspector, so the retrofit displaces it rather than adding to it. The aft cargo and tail cone wiring crosses the fitting area at three bracket stations and the wiring sheet requires re-support rather than re-clipping when a bracket station is disturbed. The existing bulletin covers the production standard only and needs a retrofit effectivity written against utilisation rather than against serial number.
sections.next_steps: Build the retrofit as a deep maintenance package that absorbs the scheduled bulkhead inspection rather than competing with it, and quote it that way. Ask the structures office to state whether the fitting jig can register on a doubled bulkhead web, and hold the answer for the doubler candidate's own review. Commission a wiring re-support scheme for the three bracket stations. Write the retrofit effectivity against accumulated flight cycles.

similarity_seeds: forged attachment fitting replacement on a stabiliser front spar
tail cone access shared between structural tasks
bracket station re-support after structural work

tasks.title: Search candidate structural work needing rear pressure bulkhead access
Map the scheduled inspection programme against the retrofit access
Assess wiring bracket stations crossing the fitting area
Draft the retrofit effectivity basis with in-service engineering

expected_findings.rationale: The candidate bulkhead web doubler works on the surface the fitting jig registers against and uses the same machined item. If both are embodied, the order matters: a doubled web changes the registration datum and the fitting cannot be set from it.
expected_findings.resolution: Obtain a written position on jig registration against a doubled web and pass it to the doubler's own review.

expected_findings.rationale: The scheduled bulkhead inspection uses the same access, the same staging and the same qualified inspector as the retrofit. Treated as separate events they compete; treated as one package the inspection is absorbed at no extra ground time.
expected_findings.resolution: Build the retrofit as a deep maintenance package that includes the inspection.

expected_findings.rationale: The tail cone wiring crosses the fitting area at three bracket stations. The wiring sheet requires a disturbed bracket station to be re-supported rather than re-clipped, which is design work and cannot be written as a bulletin step.
expected_findings.resolution: Commission a re-support scheme for the three bracket stations before the bulletin is drafted.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin was written for the production standard and states effectivity by serial number. The population that needs the retrofit is defined by accumulated cycles, not by build order, so the statement cannot be extended as it stands.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-write the retrofit effectivity against accumulated flight cycles.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the tail cone zone and reads as a reinforcing plate installation in almost the same words, but it is a crack stop repair on the bulkhead web itself. It shares no fitting item and no attachment interface with the stabiliser front spar, and an aircraft carrying it is not affected by the fitting standard.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a positive position. The retrofit is viable as a deep maintenance package; the jig registration question against a doubled web was handed to the doubler candidate rather than held here.
